task.claim:
Let n >= 1, let K = F_{2^n}, and let Tr : K -> F_2 be the absolute trace,
Tr(z) = z + z^2 + z^4 + ... + z^(2^(n-1)).

(a) TRACE-FROBENIUS. For all mu, t in K,
        Tr(mu * t^2) = Tr(mu^(1/2) * t),
    where mu^(1/2) denotes the unique square root of mu in K (squaring is a
    bijection on a field of characteristic 2). This follows from the standard
    identity Tr(z) = Tr(z^2) applied to z = mu^(1/2) * t.

(b) THE WITNESS. Let x_R in K be nonzero and set mu = x_R^(-2). Then
        mu^(1/2) + mu * x_R = 0.
    Proof: mu^(1/2) = x_R^(-1) and mu * x_R = x_R^(-2) * x_R = x_R^(-1), and
    the field has characteristic 2, so the sum is zero. Moreover mu = x_R^(-2)
    is the ONLY nonzero element of K satisfying this equation: squaring
    mu^(1/2) = mu * x_R gives mu = mu^2 * x_R^2, i.e. mu * (1 + mu * x_R^2) = 0.

(c) CONSEQUENCE. With mu = x_R^(-2), for every t in K,
        Tr( mu * ( t^2 + t * x_R ) ) = Tr( (mu^(1/2) + mu * x_R) * t ) = 0.

The cryptographic reading, which is NOT part of the formal statement: the
degree-2 coefficients of the Weil restriction of S_3(x_1, x_2, x_R) with
x_1, x_2 ranging over an F_2-subspace V with basis v_1..v_n' are exactly
c_{jk} = t^2 + t * x_R with t = v_j v_k. By (c) the F_2-linear functional
Tr(x_R^(-2) * -) annihilates all of them simultaneously, for EVERY n, every
n' and every V. So that F_2-combination of the descended equations has no
degree-2 part: a degree fall at degree 2 exists uniformly.
